flags: RECOMMENDATION (Brown Park resolution): re-point 5616 to Brown Park (north) and let it stand for both loops. The stored data already describe the north park (30 electric sites 20/30/50A, flush toilets, showers, from the Brown Park page), only the name, website and pin are South's. The county says 'Brown Park & Brown Park South are connected and share the same address at 71693 483rd Ave'; the loops are ~400 m apart off the same road, so they fall under the don't-split rule (separate places ~1 km+ with their own entrance). Full new-entry data for South are in the batch report if the reviewer prefers both.

PIN MOVE (~380 m): stored 43.52350,-95.10760 sits at the east edge of the South loop beside 483rd Ave; Brown Park's wooded campground loop is centred about 43.5269,-95.1088 (between Pearl Lake to the west and 483rd Ave/Loon Lake to the east). Brown Park South's open loop and four cabins are centred about 43.5236,-95.1087 (cabins ~43.5221,-95.1076). The county's map embed places the shared address at 43.526426,-95.108953, between the two.

RENAME and WEBSITE: 'Brown Park South' -> 'Brown Park'; website -> https://jacksoncountymn.gov/index.asp?SEC=D6820B32-0AFC-444A-8F52-184C985155BE. Phone none -> 507-849-7251 (Parks page 'Phone: 507-849-7251'). apply.py writes none of these.

WATERFRONT lakefront -> lakeview for both loops. North: the loop's west-side sites sit ~25-35 m from Pearl Lake behind a dense band of trees, the east side ~40 m from Loon Lake across 483rd Ave and a tree line: a view at best. South: the back-in pads on the east side of the loop end ~55 m (north end) to ~110 m (south end) from Loon Lake, with a trail, 483rd Ave and a tree band between: lakeview. The stored evidence ('open grass apron to the waterline, no buffer') misses the road and trees. No site numbers: ResNexus (hCaptcha) was not opened and the county publishes no site map, so no site can be named as on the water.

South's sites: on imagery the South loop is open grass with ~18 gravel back-in spurs of roughly 15-25 m off a one-way gravel loop, with a camper and an RV parked on two of them, so drive-in sites a 23-ft rig fits look likely; whether they have electric is not stated anywhere read. Brown Park's '30 trailer campsites' fit trailers by name.

Hookups not rewritten: electric 50 is confirmed by the Brown Park page ('20-amp, 30-amp and 50-amp'); the stored water/sewer (derived from the old note's '4 full-hookup') are not on either park page, only as county-wide fee categories. Left as stored, unconfirmed.
